probes.limitation: Partial control. The subagent-skip pass case is deterministic and stdin-controlled; the injection trip case is state-throttled and cannot be forced from stdin. waivers.reason: Not stdin-reachable, and separately disarmed in this environment. (a) The deny is a pure function of the on-disk state file .claude/hooks/_state/mcp-circuit-breaker.json (at least 3 failure timestamps for the server inside a 600s window, or an unexpired tripped_at). The event payload supplies only the server name via tool_name, so no stdin object can construct the trip; a stdin-only probe would read 'silent' against a clean state file and be scored a false defect. Unlike memory-nudge.py there is no env override for the state PATH. (b) Verified out-of-band by seeding the live state file with a fake server 'probesrv' (3 timestamps seconds old), running the registered hook, then removing only that key so the rest of live state was left untouched: with MCP_HEALTH_FAIL_OPEN cleared it emitted permissionDecision 'deny' with the full breaker reason, so the hook logic is intact; with the ambient environment as-is it stayed silent at exit 0. See defects_found: MCP_HEALTH_FAIL_OPEN=1 is set at Windows User scope, so every hook subprocess inherits it and the deny branch is unreachable in a live session.

Not stdin-reachable. _handle_session_start reads nothing from the payload beyond hook_event_name; it fires only when the counter file (.claude/hooks/_state/memory-nudge.json, or MEMORY_NUDGE_STATE_PATH) satisfies turns_since_memory_write >= 10 AND turns minus turns_at_last_nudge >= 10. A stdin-only probe therefore reads whatever the live counter holds that minute, which is non-deterministic, and firing it against live state consumes the user's pending nudge by stamping turns_at_last_nudge. The live file stood at turns=12 / watermark=0 during this batch, meaning one real nudge was pending, so I deliberately did not fire it. Verified out-of-band with MEMORY_NUDGE_STATE_PATH pointed at a temp file: seeded {turns:12, watermark:0} produced the SessionStart additionalContext '[MEMORY PERSISTENCE] 12 main-session turns have closed...' at exit 0, and seeded {turns:3} was silent at exit 0. This becomes probeable if the probe schema gains an env or state-seed field.

defects_found.detail: The breaker cannot deny in this environment. MCP_HEALTH_FAIL_OPEN=1 is set as a Windows USER-scope environment variable ([Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('MCP_HEALTH_FAIL_OPEN','User') returns 1; Machine scope is empty), so every hook subprocess Claude Code spawns inherits it and _is_override_set() returns True on every evaluation. Proven by running the registered hook against a state file seeded with 3 failures seconds old: with the inherited environment it printed nothing and exited 0; with identical state and stdin under 'env -u MCP_HEALTH_FAIL_OPEN' it printed permissionDecision deny. The documented purpose of that variable is a per-call escape hatch (bypass the breaker for the next call), not a standing setting. This is the audit's own pattern: registered, green sibling tests (test_mcp_circuit_breaker.py sets and clears the variable inside the test process, so the suite never sees the ambient one), and zero enforcement. The fix is an environment change, not a code change, so it is reported and not applied.

Not an enforcement defect, a classifier hazard for the merged suite: this hook blocks with stdout {"decision":"block"} at exit code 0. A runner that defines 'block' as exit code 2 (the taxonomy in the authoring brief) scores every trip of this hook as a mere 'warn', and would score a gutted version that printed any stray line as equally green. The suite must read the decision field for Stop-event hooks.

Three of the five controls in this batch (mcp-circuit-breaker.py, memory-nudge.py, and the fire path of user-prompt-state-inject.py) gate on an on-disk state file rather than on the event payload, so a stdin-only probe cannot construct their trip and would score a working hook as silent. Two are waived here for exactly that reason. If the probe schema gained a per-probe 'env' map and a 'state_seed' (path plus JSON body written before the run and restored after), all three become genuinely probeable; memory-nudge.py already exposes MEMORY_NUDGE_STATE_PATH for this, mcp-circuit-breaker.py exposes no state-path override at all.
